record.paper_title: Resolution of Some Open Problems Concerning Multiple Zeta Evaluations of Arbitrary Depth
record.context_brief: General depth-reduction problem for multiple zeta values
record.original_question: For each positive integer k, let Z_k denote the set of all multiple zeta values with positive integer arguments and depth less than k. Given positive integers s_1, …, s_k with s_1 > 1 so that ζ(s_1, …, s_k) converges, determine for which k-tuples (s_1, …, s_k) the depth-k multiple zeta value ζ(s_1, …, s_k) lies in the polynomial ring Q[Z_k], meaning that it can be expressed by a rational polynomial relation in multiple zeta values of smaller depth.

evidence.quote: For each positive integer k, let Zk denote the set of all multiple zeta values (with positive integer arguments) of depth less than k. If we restrict our attention to rational polynomial relationships, the aforementioned problem amounts to determining for each k the values of the arguments s1; ... ;sk for which the sum (1) lies in the polynomial ring Q[Zk]. Settling this question in complete generality is currently well beyond the reach of number theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A multiple zeta value (MZV) is defined, for positive integers s_1, s_2, …, s_k with s_1 ≥ 2 (so that the series converges), by
  ζ(s_1, s_2, …, s_k) = ∑_{n_1 > n_2 > … > n_k ≥ 1} 1 / (n_1^{s_1} n_2^{s_2} ⋯ n_k^{s_k}).
The integer k is called the depth and s_1 + … + s_k is called the weight.

For each positive integer k, let Z_k denote the set of all multiple zeta values whose depth is strictly less than k (including, by convention, the rationals at depth 0). Let Q[Z_k] denote the Q-subalgebra of R generated by Z_k, i.e. the set of all rational polynomial expressions in elements of Z_k.

Problem. Determine, for every k ≥ 1, the precise set of admissible tuples (s_1, …, s_k) of positive integers with s_1 ≥ 2 for which
  ζ(s_1, s_2, …, s_k) ∈ Q[Z_k],
that is, characterize all depth-k multiple zeta values that can be written as a polynomial with rational coefficients in multiple zeta values of strictly smaller depth.
artifact.status_search_result: The general depth-reduction problem for multiple zeta values—deciding precisely which admissible tuples (s_1,…,s_k) yield ζ(s_1,…,s_k) expressible as a Q-polynomial in MZVs of lower depth—remains open. Substantial partial results exist (e.g., parity theorems, sum formulas, Ohno–Zagier type identities, depth reductions in special families such as ζ(1,…,1,2m̄) for alternating MZVs, and the conjectural depth-graded picture via period polynomials of cusp forms for SL_2(Z) due to Broadhurst–Kreimer and others), but a complete classification is not known and is widely regarded as out of reach of current techniques.

status_evidence.title: Differential operators and a depth reduction for the alternating multiple zeta values
status_evidence.snippet: Studies depth reduction for special alternating multiple zeta values, showing that depth reduction beyond known families is an active research problem.
status_evidence.claim: Depth reduction is studied case by case; no general classification is available.

status_evidence.title: Depth-graded motivic multiple zeta values (Compositio Math.)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides conjectural description of relations modulo lower depth in terms of period polynomials of cusp forms for SL_2(Z); conjectures remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The complete structure of MZVs modulo lower depth is conjectural and unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Multiple zeta values – tasting notes (W. Zudilin)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey indicating that determining all polynomial relations among MZVs, in particular depth reductions, contains many open conjectures.
